- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days — cap forecast at +3–5% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (avg > -0.1), model underestimates upward momentum — add 2–4% to forecast mean for next 7 days.
- Model frequently overestimates short-term volatility — smooth 30d forecast by averaging last 7–10 days’ values before final 10–15 days.
- When sentiment turns positive after negative streak, model delays reaction — forecast should rise 1–2 days ahead of sentiment shift.
- If last 3–5 days show strong mean reversion (price moving back toward 30d MA), model tends to overpredict continuation — reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 5 days.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model often misses tail risk — add 1–3% buffer for extreme upward moves if sentiment > 0.2 over last 7 days.
